conceptual assets.concept: Spinlock stored state (lock_q) — the per-bit stored lock values
conceptual assets.reasoning: lock_q is declared as the 32-bit storage for each hardware lock, is reset in the spinlock process (`if (rstn_i = '0') then lock_q(i) <= '0'`), and is updated on clock edges when the request-targeting conditions hold (`elsif rising_edge(clk_i) then if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1') then lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw;`). The bus_response process reads lock_q (masked by sel when addr(7)='0' or the full vector when addr(7)='1') into the external response. Flows that read or update locks therefore depend on the integrity of lock_q; corruption would make read/update behavior incorrect. The declared signal lock_q is the storing element realizing this concept.

conceptual assets.concept: Selected lock index (sel) — address decode that targets which lock bit is accessed
conceptual assets.reasoning: sel(i) is computed locally by the concurrent assignment `sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(i, 5))) else '0'`. The spinlock update condition explicitly depends on sel(i) and the read path masks lock_q with sel (`bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel` when addr(7)='0'). Therefore the correctness (integrity) of the selection decode determines which bit is read or written; corruption of sel would direct reads/updates to the wrong bit. The declared signal sel is the combinational element computing this selection.
